operations.description:
Delete a product from active marketplace use.

This operation removes a product from search results, category listings, and other customer-facing browsing surfaces. It is intended for sellers deleting their own products and for administrators enforcing platform policy.

Before deletion, the service must verify that none of the product's variants have pending order items in paid or shipped status, and that none of the variants have pending cancellation requests or refund requests. If any of those conditions are not satisfied, the request must fail and the product must remain unchanged.

When deletion succeeds, the product's variants are removed from active use and their inventory records are also removed from active use. Snapshot history must remain preserved so authorized sellers and administrators can review past product states for disputes and audit purposes. Deleting a product must not break order history or historical snapshot references.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the product by productId and authorize the caller as either the owning seller or an administrator.

Reject the request with not found when the product does not exist. Reject with forbidden when the caller is neither the owner nor an administrator with product oversight authority.

Before deleting, check all variants of the product for any order items whose status is paid or shipped, and for any pending cancellation or refund requests. If any blocking record exists, reject the request with a business validation error and do not modify the database.

If validation passes, delete the product in a transaction together with its variants and any inventory records tied to those variants. The delete should remove them from active use, not from preserved snapshot history tables. After commit, ensure any derived browse/index caches are refreshed so the product no longer appears in search or category listings.

Do not attempt to delete or rewrite snapshot tables. Historical snapshots must remain queryable for authorized dispute review.

operations.description:
Update the ordered image set for a product.

This operation lets the seller who owns the product maintain the product’s presentation by adding images, reordering them, or removing images as part of one product-scoped update. The first image in the final order becomes the main thumbnail used in listings and product detail pages.

Only the owning seller may use this endpoint. The server must reject requests for products that do not belong to the authenticated seller, and it must preserve the product’s existing image state when validation fails or when any target image is unavailable. Successful changes must be recorded in the product snapshot history so the previous and updated image order can be reviewed later for disputes or audit purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the product by productId and confirm the authenticated seller owns it. Treat this as a product-image maintenance command over the product's ordered image set. Apply the requested image changes atomically so partial reorder/delete/add operations do not leave the gallery in a mixed state.

Validate that every referenced image belongs to the target product, that any reorder request covers only existing images, and that unavailable targets are rejected as business errors. If the request adds images, create new product image rows tied to the product and insert them in the requested order. If it reorders images, persist the new ordering and make the first item the main image. If it removes images, delete only the specified product image rows after confirming they still exist and belong to the product.

After a successful change, create the corresponding product snapshot entry that captures the previous and new image state together with the rest of the product's editable data. On any validation or business-rule failure, roll back all database changes and do not create a snapshot. Return the updated product image collection in paginated summary form consistent with the index operation contract.

The system should verify that both the product and image exist, that the image belongs to the given product, and that the caller is allowed to view the product's image data. If the product or image cannot be found, or if the image is not associated with the specified product, the request should fail with a normal business not-found error.

Load the product by `productId`, then load the image by `imageId` constrained to `mall_platform_product_images.mall_platform_product_id = productId`.

Return the single product image record with its id, product id, image URL, sort order, main-image flag, created timestamp, updated timestamp, and deleted timestamp if applicable. Do not return images from other products.

If the product does not exist, the image does not exist, or the image does not belong to the specified product, return a not-found style business error. Apply the same product access restrictions used elsewhere in the product image feature so unauthorized users cannot infer image existence across products. No write side effects are required.

operations.description:
Add a new image to a product.

This operation lets the owning seller attach an additional image to an existing product so the product can be presented with a richer image gallery. The inserted image becomes part of the product's ordered image set, and the first image in that order serves as the thumbnail used in listings.

The target product must exist and belong to the authenticated seller. The request is rejected if the product is missing, belongs to another seller, or violates image-management validation such as duplicate image URLs or conflicting display order. Image creation is part of product maintenance, and the result is immediately visible on the product detail page according to its display order.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the target product by productId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated seller. Reject the request with a business error if the product does not exist or if the caller is not the owner.

Insert a new row into mall_platform_product_images using the target product id, the submitted image URL, the intended sort order, and the is_main flag. Enforce the unique constraints on (mall_platform_product_id, image_url) and (mall_platform_product_id, sort_order). If the same image URL already exists for the product, return a conflict-style business validation error rather than creating a duplicate. If the requested sort order is already occupied, either shift ordering in a controlled transaction or reject the request according to the implementation rules, but never leave the gallery in a partially updated state.

If the product currently has no images, make the inserted image the main image. If the product already has a main image, preserve the existing thumbnail behavior unless the chosen ordering logic explicitly promotes the new row. Do not change unrelated products. Because product image history is preserved through snapshots, ensure the surrounding product update flow records the change where appropriate. Return the created image record after persistence.

Update one image that belongs to a product.

The request is validated against product ownership and image availability. If the product does not exist, is not owned by the caller, or the target image is no longer available for that product, the request is rejected and no unrelated images are modified. The previous state must be preserved in the product image snapshot history before the update is committed.

Load the product by productId and verify that the authenticated seller owns it. Then load the target image by imageId scoped to that product. Reject the request if the product is missing, the image is missing, the product is not owned by the caller, or the product is unavailable for image maintenance.

Apply only the fields allowed by the product image update DTO. Do not allow reassignment to another product. If the update changes ordering or other presentation attributes, keep the image set consistent so the first image remains the thumbnail used in listings. Before persisting the update, create the corresponding product image snapshot entry that preserves the prior image state.

Use a transaction so the snapshot insert and the image update are atomic. If the target image is unavailable, return a business error and do not reorder or delete any other images as a side effect.

Delete one image from a seller-owned product.

This operation removes a single image from the product's ordered image set. If the deleted image was the first image, the next image in order becomes the new thumbnail used in listings. If it was the only image, the product remains without a thumbnail until a new image is added.

Only the seller who owns the product may perform this action. The request must fail if the product does not exist, is no longer available for image maintenance, or the target image cannot be found under that product. When the action is rejected, the existing image list must remain unchanged.

The deletion must be captured in history through the product image snapshot mechanism so the previous presentation can be reconstructed for audit and dispute review.

Resolve the target image by imageId within the scope of that product only; if it is missing, return a business not-found error and do not modify any other image rows.
Execute the removal in a transaction, then preserve the remaining image ordering so the product keeps a stable visual sequence.
If the deleted image was the main thumbnail, promote the next image in order to thumbnail; if it was the last image, leave the product without a thumbnail.
Record the removed state in the product image snapshot/history tables before committing, and return no response body on success.

operations.description:
List the variants that belong to a specific product.

This endpoint returns the product's variant records in a paginated collection so callers can inspect SKU code, option values, pricing, and current availability for the selected product. A product may have multiple variants, and a product with no variants remains visible elsewhere in the platform but is not purchasable.

The result is always scoped to the product identified by the path parameter. Search, pagination, and sorting are supplied in the request body, and callers should expect an empty page when the product exists but has no variants. If the product cannot be found, the service should return the standard not-found error. If the caller is not allowed to access the product's variants, the service should return the standard forbidden error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Verify that the target product exists, then query mall_platform_product_variants using product_id as the scope filter.

Support the shared list request conventions for pagination, keyword search, and sorting. Search should be applied against variant-facing fields that are useful in list views, such as SKU code and option values, while preserving deterministic sorting for stable pagination.

Return a summary projection for each row rather than the full entity. The summary should be composed only from fields that exist in the product variant schema and related data that is explicitly available in the persistence model. Do not invent stock or availability fields; derive them only from persisted variant and inventory data if those fields are available to the implementation layer.

If the product does not exist, return not found. If access is denied, return forbidden. If there are no matching variants, return an empty page with the requested pagination metadata. This operation must not mutate product, variant, inventory, or snapshot data.

The variant must belong to the specified product. If the product does not exist, the variant does not exist, or the identifiers do not match, the service should return a not-found response. If the caller is not allowed to view the product or variant because of account status or visibility rules, the service should return the appropriate authorization or visibility error.

Resolve the parent product first, then query mall_platform_product_variants using both the product ID and the variant ID so the lookup is constrained to the parent scope. Reject mismatched parent-child combinations even when the variant exists under another product.

Return the full current product variant entity only. Do not include inventory history, snapshot history, or parent product images in this response. If either record cannot be found, return a not-found result. If the product is hidden, suspended, or otherwise inaccessible to the caller, return the appropriate authorization or visibility failure based on the caller's role and the product's state.

This operation is read-only and must not mutate stock, availability, or any snapshot tables.

Creates a new variant for the specified product.

This operation allows the owning seller to add a purchasable SKU variant beneath an existing product, including its option values and optional price override. The product must exist and must belong to the authenticated seller.

The SKU code must be unique across all variants. If the product previously had no variants, this creation restores the possibility of purchase once inventory is added and the variant is active. Unauthorized access, missing products, and duplicate SKU codes must be rejected with the appropriate errors.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId and verify that it exists. Confirm the authenticated seller owns the product and is allowed to modify it.

Validate the request payload against the product variant rules. The SKU code is required and must be globally unique. Option values must describe the variant combination, and any optional price override must be a valid catalog price. Do not accept client-provided identifiers, owner fields, timestamps, or stock totals.

Insert the new row into mall_platform_product_variants linked to the product. If the implementation persists snapshots for editable commerce entities on create, store the initial snapshot in the same transaction so the original variant state is preserved. Return conflict for duplicate SKU codes, not-found for missing products, and forbidden when the seller does not own the product.

Update a product variant that belongs to a specific product.

This operation lets the owning seller edit one variant’s SKU code, option values, and optional price override within the specified product. The product context is taken from the path, so the variant cannot be moved to another product through this operation.

The service must verify that the authenticated seller owns the parent product and that the target variant belongs to that product. It must also enforce SKU code uniqueness across all product variants. If the SKU code is already in use by another variant, the update must be rejected and no changes should be persisted.

Because the platform preserves all money-related changes for dispute review and historical reconstruction, the previous variant state must be written to a snapshot before the update is committed. If the product or variant cannot be found, return a not-found error. If the caller is not authorized to edit the product, return an authorization error. If SKU uniqueness is violated, return a validation or conflict error according to platform conventions.

Fetch the product by productId and confirm it exists. Then fetch the variant by variantId and verify it belongs to that product. Confirm the authenticated seller owns the product and has permission to edit it.

Validate the update payload against product variant rules. Apply only mutable fields: SKU code, option values, and optional price override. Do not allow reassignment to a different product or modification of immutable identifiers.

Enforce global SKU uniqueness on mall_platform_product_variants. If the SKU code changes, check for collisions against other variants before writing. If the SKU remains unchanged, allow the update to proceed.

Create a product variant snapshot containing the current persisted state before applying the update. Perform the snapshot insert and the update in a single transaction so the historical record and live record remain consistent.

Return the refreshed updated variant entity after commit. Use 404 for missing product or variant, 403 for ownership or authorization failure, and 409 or the platform’s standard validation error for SKU conflicts.

Delete one variant from a product.

This operation removes a single variant from the specified product after verifying that the variant belongs to that product and that the caller is allowed to manage the product. It is intended for seller-managed catalog maintenance and should only affect the targeted variant.

Deletion is blocked if any related order items are still pending in paid or shipped status, or if any cancellation requests or refund requests are still pending for that variant. When the request is rejected for one of these dependency reasons, no active records should be changed.

When deletion succeeds, the variant is removed from active purchase selection and its inventory records are taken out of active use according to the product lifecycle rules. Historical snapshots and preserved order history remain available for authorized review.

Verify that the product exists and that the variant belongs to the product before attempting deletion. Enforce seller ownership or equivalent product-management authorization.

Check for blocking dependencies on the target variant: any order items in paid or shipped status, any pending cancellation requests, and any pending refund requests. If any blocking dependency exists, reject the operation with a conflict-style error and leave all rows unchanged.

If eligible, delete the variant in a transaction and remove its inventory records from active use. Do not delete immutable snapshots or any preserved order history. After the delete, leave product-level visibility rules to the product service; if no variants remain, the product may become unavailable for purchase as defined by domain rules.

operations.description:
Lists inventory movement records for a specific product variant.

This operation returns the append-only stock history for the requested variant so authorized users can review restocks, deductions, manual adjustments, and stock restoration events in chronological order. Because inventory records belong to one variant, the product and variant identifiers in the path define the scope of the query.

The response is intended for seller-side inventory management and administrator oversight. Results should be paginated and sortable by creation time, and the implementation should reject requests when the variant does not belong to the given product or when the caller is not allowed to inspect that product's inventory history.

operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId and verify it exists and is active for the requested scope. Then load the variant by variantId and ensure it belongs to the given product; if not, return a not-found or invalid-scope error. Query mall_platform_inventory_records filtered by mall_platform_product_variant_id, and apply pagination and sorting from the request body.

Support browsing filters suitable for inventory history, such as created_at date range, reason text search, and quantity change direction if the request DTO includes them. Order results by created_at according to the requested sort, defaulting to newest-first for history review. Do not modify inventory records in this operation; it is strictly read-only. If the caller lacks permission to inspect this product's inventory, return an authorization error. If no records exist, return an empty page rather than an error.

Retrieve a single inventory movement record for a specific product variant.

This endpoint returns one historical stock change entry within the scope of the specified product and variant. The record represents an append-only inventory event and includes the signed quantity change, the business reason for the movement, and the timestamps associated with the record.

The inventory record must belong to the requested variant, and the variant must belong to the requested product. If any identifier is invalid, or if the identifiers do not match across the product, variant, and inventory record relationships, the request must fail with a not-found response. Use relational checks or joins against mall_platform_products and mall_platform_product_variants to prevent cross-product access. Return not found if the product, variant, or inventory record does not exist, or if the ownership chain is broken. Do not compute current stock here; this endpoint returns only the stored inventory history row. Return the schema-backed fields: id, mall_platform_product_variant_id, quantity_change, reason, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

This operation appends a stock movement entry to the variant’s inventory history instead of modifying prior records. The recorded change is used to derive the variant’s current stock and availability state, including out-of-stock behavior in product browsing and cart validation.

The product and variant in the path must belong together. If the product does not exist, the variant does not exist, or the variant is not owned by the referenced product, the request must fail without creating any inventory data. Wrap the insert in a transaction. If validation fails or the insert cannot be completed, roll back the transaction so the stock position remains unchanged. Enforce the inventory record schema rules for quantity change and reason fields, and allow the caller to record both positive restocks and negative adjustments where permitted by business rules.

List the historical snapshots for a product's images.

The history is scoped to one product identified in the path. Only successful image changes appear in the results; failed image operations do not create snapshots and therefore do not appear here. Because image order affects listing presentation, each snapshot should preserve the image ordering and main image state as captured at the time of the successful change.

Do not synthesize snapshot entries from the current image state. Return only snapshots that were created after successful image changes, and preserve the historical ordering and main-image selection recorded in each snapshot.

operations.description:
Retrieve one historical image snapshot for a product.

This endpoint returns the immutable record of a product image at the moment it was captured, including the image URL, display order, main-image flag, and timestamps. It is intended for seller maintenance review, administrator oversight, and dispute investigation where the exact visual state of a product must be examined.

The snapshot is scoped to a single product, so the product identifier and snapshot identifier must refer to the same parent-child relationship in storage. If the product does not exist, the snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot belongs to another product, the request must fail with a not-found error. The operation does not modify data and does not create a new snapshot.

If the product does not exist, the snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot belongs to another product, the request must fail with a not-found error. The operation does not modify data and does not create a new snapshot.

operations.description:
Lists the immutable snapshot history for all variants of a product.

This endpoint returns paginated summaries of variant snapshot records that belong to the specified product. It is used to review preserved SKU code changes, option value changes, price changes, and the timestamp of each recorded edit for dispute resolution and historical auditing.

Because variant snapshots are immutable history records, this operation is read-only and does not allow creating, updating, or deleting snapshot data. The product scope ensures the result set stays limited to a single product’s variant history. If the product does not exist, the service must return a not-found error. If the caller is not authorized to view the product’s snapshot history, the service must return an authorization error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the product by productId first, then verify the caller is allowed to view its variant snapshot history according to ownership and administrator access rules. Query mall_platform_product_variant_snapshots for snapshots related to variants of that product, and return them as immutable summary rows only.

Apply pagination, sorting, and any supported filters from the request body, such as variant identity or snapshot time range. Default ordering should be newest snapshot first. Do not modify snapshot rows, do not regenerate them, and do not expose any deletion or edit functionality. If the product is missing, return 404. If access is denied, return 403. If no history exists, return an empty page.

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated customer's active shopping cart.

This endpoint provides the current cart owned by the signed-in customer, including the cart header state and all selected cart items. It is intended for cart viewing and checkout preparation only.

Access is limited to registered customers with a valid session. If the session is missing or invalid, the request must be rejected as unauthorized. If the customer does not currently have an active cart, the service should return not found rather than creating a new cart implicitly.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the current customer from the authenticated session, then look up the single shopping cart row in mall_platform_shopping_carts that belongs to that customer and represents the active cart. Load related mall_platform_cart_items rows so the response contains the cart contents needed by the UI.

Do not accept any cart identifier from the client. The cart must be selected from the session context to prevent cross-account access. Enforce registered-customer access before querying the database. If the account is absent, banned, or otherwise not allowed to use cart functionality, return an authorization or forbidden error. If no active cart exists for the customer, return not found instead of creating one automatically.

Preserve the persisted cart state and item ordering as stored in the database.

responseBody.description: The authenticated customer's active shopping cart, including its items and checkout-preparation state.

operations.description:
Updates the authenticated customer's active shopping cart.

This endpoint applies cart changes to the current customer's singleton cart and recalculates the cart state after the update. It is intended for item quantity changes, variant additions, and item removals performed as one atomic cart operation.

The cart belongs to the current customer account, and each line item references one product variant. If a requested variant is unavailable, deleted, or cannot satisfy the requested quantity, the operation must fail without partially modifying the saved cart contents.

If the update succeeds, the service persists the changed cart items and returns the refreshed cart representation so the caller can immediately redraw the cart view.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer from the security context and resolve that customer's unique shopping cart through mall_platform_shopping_carts. Apply the request as a single transaction against mall_platform_cart_items.

Use the cart's unique customer ownership to locate the active cart. Never accept owner identifiers from the client payload. If the service requires the cart to exist before updates, create or reuse it only under the authenticated customer's context and only if that behavior is explicitly supported by the surrounding application flow.

When applying line changes, enforce the unique constraint on (mall_platform_shopping_cart_id, mall_platform_product_variant_id) so a variant is merged into an existing line instead of creating duplicates. Validate the referenced product variant against mall_platform_product_variants and reject deleted or unavailable variants. Validate quantity changes so resulting quantities remain positive and consistent with cart rules.

If the request attempts to remove a line, delete the cart-item row. If it updates quantity, update only that row and its timestamps. If it adds a variant already present in the cart, increase the existing quantity rather than inserting a second row. Preserve unchanged lines exactly as they were.

Do not mutate the cart on validation failure. Return the refreshed cart state after commit, including the items needed for UI display and any derived totals or availability markers supported by the response model.

responseBody.description: A paginated representation of the customer's refreshed active shopping cart after the requested changes are applied.

requestBody.description: Cart mutation instructions for the authenticated customer's active cart, including item additions, removals, and quantity updates.

operations.description:
Add a selected product variant to a shopping cart, merging with an existing cart line when the same variant is already present.

This operation is scoped to one shopping cart and must only be allowed for the authenticated customer who owns that cart. The cart item is identified by the combination of cart and product variant, so the service must not create duplicate lines for the same variant.

The service must validate that the cart exists, is owned by the caller, and that the referenced product variant exists and is eligible for purchase. If the variant is unavailable or the requested quantity is invalid, the request must fail without changing other cart items.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Fetch the shopping cart by id and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer. If the cart is missing or owned by another customer, reject the request.

Load the referenced product variant and verify that it exists and is currently usable for cart placement. Reject the request if the variant is deleted, inactive, or otherwise unavailable. Validate that quantity is a positive integer.

Use the unique constraint on (mall_platform_shopping_cart_id, mall_platform_product_variant_id) to determine whether a cart item already exists for the requested variant. If it exists, increase its quantity by the requested amount and update updated_at. If it does not exist, insert a new cart item with the requested quantity and an availability_state derived from the variant's current status.

Update the parent cart's updated_at after a successful merge or insert. Handle concurrent create attempts safely by re-reading the existing cart item if a unique constraint conflict occurs. Do not modify unrelated cart items when validation fails or when persistence errors occur.

responseBody.description: The created cart item, or the existing cart item after its quantity has been merged.

parameters.description: The shopping cart identifier within the authenticated customer's scope.
parameters.name: cartId

requestBody.description: Payload that identifies the product variant to add and the quantity to place into the cart.

prerequisites.description: The selected product variant must be created before it can be added to a shopping cart.

operations.description:
Lists and updates the items in a shopping cart.

This endpoint operates within the scope of one customer shopping cart and is used to view the cart contents and apply item-level quantity changes. Each cart item remains an independent line for a specific product variant, so updates must not merge or overwrite other cart items.

The service must validate cart ownership, variant availability, and quantity rules before applying any update. If the request fails, the cart contents and totals must remain unchanged. When an update succeeds, the affected item subtotal and the cart total should be recalculated consistently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer.
Use the request body to apply cart-item search, pagination, and sorting rules for the scoped cart.
If the request includes quantity adjustments, update only the targeted cart item rows for the same cart and keep each variant line isolated.
Recalculate the affected item subtotal and the cart total after a successful mutation.
Reject requests that reference unavailable variants, invalid quantities, or carts that do not belong to the caller.
Run the operation transactionally so a failure leaves every cart item unchanged and preserves the prior cart totals.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single cart item from a specific shopping cart.

This endpoint returns the cart item identified by `cartItemId` only when it belongs to the shopping cart identified by `cartId`. It is intended for cart review and checkout preparation, where the customer needs to inspect item details such as the selected variant, quantity, subtotal, and availability state.

The service must validate both identifiers together and reject mismatched ownership. If the cart does not exist, the cart item does not exist, or the item belongs to a different cart, the request should fail with a not found response. Items that are unavailable because the underlying variant was deleted or is out of stock must still be retrievable so the customer can resolve the cart before checkout.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and then load the cart item by cartItemId, verifying that the item belongs to that cart before returning it.

Query mall_platform_shopping_carts and mall_platform_cart_items only. Do not allow access to cart items from another cart even if the item identifier exists. Return a not-found error when the cart is missing, the cart item is missing, or the ownership relation does not match.

Include the related product variant context needed by the cart UI to render item name, option values, unit price, quantity, subtotal, and availability state. If the variant is deleted or out of stock, still return the cart item so the customer can see what must be removed or adjusted before checkout. This operation must not modify cart state or inventory state.

operations.description:
Update a cart item inside a shopping cart.

This operation changes one line item that belongs to the specified cart. It is intended for customer cart edits before checkout, such as changing the quantity of a selected product variant, while keeping the rest of the cart intact.

The service must verify that the cart item exists under the cart identified by {cartId} and that the caller is allowed to modify that cart. If the cart or item is missing, the operation must fail with a not found error. If the requested change violates cart rules or product-variant availability constraints, the operation must fail with a validation error and leave the cart unchanged.

On success, the updated cart item is returned so the client can refresh the displayed cart line, subtotal, and any stock warnings derived from the current saved state.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and confirm it belongs to the authenticated customer. Then load the cart item by cartItemId within that cart scope; reject the request if the item does not belong to the cart.

Apply only fields defined by IMallPlatformCartItem.IUpdate. Do not permit updates to the cart reference, item identity, or other immutable context fields through the request body. Validate mutable values, especially quantity, against cart rules and the current availability of the referenced product variant. If the new quantity is invalid, below the minimum allowed, or conflicts with business constraints, return a validation error and do not persist partial changes.

If the referenced variant is unavailable or no longer valid, return an appropriate business error when the requested update cannot be applied safely. Recompute any cart-derived totals and availability warnings from persisted cart data after the update is saved. Use a transaction so the item update and any dependent recalculations remain consistent. Return 404 for missing cart or cart item, 403 for carts owned by another customer, and 422 for business-rule violations.

responseBody.description: The cart item after the update has been applied.

parameters.description: The shopping cart identifier that scopes the cart item.

operations.description:
Remove one item from a shopping cart.

This operation deletes the selected cart line identified by the cart item within the specified cart. It only affects that cart entry, recalculates the cart state, and leaves all other items unchanged. If the item is not present, the request is handled safely and the cart remains unchanged.

The operation is scoped to the referenced cart and must not affect items belonging to another cart. The cart total is updated after removal, and the deleted item is no longer shown in the cart view.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and verify the cart item belongs to that cart through mall_platform_cart_items.mall_platform_shopping_cart_id. Delete only the matching cart item row; do not touch other rows in the cart.

Use the cart item membership check and deletion in a single transaction when possible. If the cart item does not exist or is not attached to the specified cart, treat the request as a safe no-op success to satisfy the cart removal requirement.

After deletion, any cart totals or subtotals must be recalculated by the cart read/query layer because the schema shown here does not store derived totals on the cart header. Do not assume additional balance or total columns exist. Preserve consistency with the product variant relation so that only the selected variant line is removed.

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated customer's wishlist as a paginated list of saved products.

This endpoint provides the customer-facing browsing view for wishlist content. Each result represents a saved product rather than a variant-level entry, so customers can revisit products they marked for later consideration. Deleted products must not appear in the response because wishlist maintenance keeps saved items aligned with products that still exist in the catalog.

Access is limited to registered customer accounts and the wishlist owned by the current customer. The service must enforce ownership checks and return an authorization error if the caller is not an authenticated customer. The response is intended for repeat browsing and should support pagination and sorting consistent with wishlist browsing behavior.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Verify that the caller is an authenticated customer before reading wishlist data.

Load the wishlist entries owned by the current customer and join them to the related product records so the response can present browsable saved products. Exclude any entries whose products were deleted, because wishlist cleanup rules require deleted products to be removed from all wishlists and they must not appear in browsing results.

Return a paginated result set using the platform page type pattern. Keep ordering stable for the customer experience, and return an empty page when the customer has no saved products. Do not expose any wishlist records belonging to other customers.

responseBody.description: Paginated wishlist browsing results containing the authenticated customer's saved products.

operations.description:
Create the authenticated customer’s wishlist container.

This operation initializes the one wishlist resource owned by the signed-in customer so saved products can be managed at the product level. The wishlist belongs to the customer account and is used for later product-interest browsing rather than immediate purchase.

Only registered customer accounts may use this operation. If the customer already has a wishlist, the request must fail instead of creating a duplicate container. The wishlist itself does not store product selections; those are handled by wishlist item records.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticate the caller as a customer and resolve the owner from the security context. Do not accept any owner identifier from the client. Check mall_platform_wishlists for an existing row for the current customer account; if one exists, return a conflict-style error and do not insert another record.

If no wishlist exists, insert a new wishlist row linked to the authenticated customer and return the persisted entity. Enforce customer-only access; unauthenticated callers and non-customer actors must be rejected. Do not create wishlist items here. Keep the implementation consistent with the one-wishlist-per-customer rule implied by the domain model and wishlist operations.

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist owned by the authenticated customer.

requestBody.description: No client-provided fields are required because the wishlist owner is derived from the authenticated customer context.

operations.description:
Updates the authenticated customer's wishlist contents.

This endpoint lets a registered customer maintain the list of products saved for later consideration. Wishlist entries are stored at the product level, so each saved item represents a product rather than a specific variant.

Only the owning customer may use this operation. The update must be processed atomically so that a failure leaves the existing wishlist unchanged. If a referenced product no longer exists, the request should be rejected instead of preserving a stale wishlist entry.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated customer and load that customer's wishlist container. Validate that the request contains product references only and does not attempt to store variant-level data.

Apply the wishlist changes in a single transaction so that any validation or persistence failure leaves the current saved products unchanged. Deduplicate repeated product references if necessary. Reject requests from unauthenticated callers and from non-customer actors.

If the customer's wishlist container is created lazily in this service, create it as part of the transaction; otherwise, update the existing container only. Ensure deleted products cannot remain in the final saved list because wishlist maintenance must not expose catalog items that no longer exist.

responseBody.description: The customer's wishlist after the saved-product update has been successfully applied.

requestBody.description: Wishlist update payload containing the customer's saved products. The list must reference products only and must not include product variants.

operations.description:
Delete the current customer's wishlist.

This operation removes the authenticated customer's wishlist container and all saved product entries in it. It does not affect any product records, product variants, or other customers' wishlists.

The request is scoped to the current authenticated customer account. The service must verify ownership before removing the wishlist data. If the wishlist does not exist, the operation should be treated as idempotent and succeed without changing other data.

If the customer has saved items, they are removed together with the wishlist so the account no longer has a persisted wishlist state. Catalog data remains unchanged, and future product deletions continue to be handled by the automatic cleanup rules elsewhere in the system.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer identity from the session context, then locate the wishlist owned by that customer.
If no wishlist exists for the customer, return success without modifying other records.
If a wishlist exists, delete the wishlist record and its dependent wishlist item rows in the same transaction to avoid orphaned entries.
Do not delete or modify any product rows, category rows, or customer profile rows.
Enforce ownership so one customer cannot delete another customer's wishlist.
Return no response body on success. If the customer is not authenticated or does not own the targeted wishlist context, respond with the appropriate authorization error.

operations.description:
Browse the authenticated customer's saved products in their wishlist.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of product-level wishlist entries for the signed-in customer. It is intended for personal product-interest browsing and should reflect only products that still exist in the catalog.

Search, sorting, and pagination are supported for a usable wishlist view. If a saved product has been deleted, it must not appear in the result set. The service must only return the authenticated customer's own saved items and must not expose other customers' wishlists.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Identify the authenticated customer and query mall_platform_wishlist_items through the owning mall_platform_wishlists record for that customer. Join against products so deleted products are excluded from browsing results and current product data can be used for summaries.

Implement search, pagination, and sorting in the request body. Search should target product-level fields appropriate for wishlist browsing. Return an empty page when the customer has no saved products. Do not allow cross-customer access; the authenticated principal determines the scope.

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation creates one saved-product entry in the current customer's wishlist. Wishlist items are tracked at the product level, so the request saves a product only and does not store a variant selection.

The service resolves the caller's wishlist from the authenticated customer, validates that the product still exists, and rejects duplicate saves for the same product within the same wishlist. If the product has already been removed from the catalog, the request fails and no saved items are changed.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated customer account and locate the customer's wishlist through mall_platform_wishlists.customer_id. Insert one mall_platform_wishlist_items row for the requested product after confirming the product exists in mall_platform_products.

Enforce the unique constraint on (mall_platform_wishlist_id, mall_platform_product_id) so a product can be saved only once per wishlist. Reject duplicate requests with a conflict-style error rather than updating existing rows. Do not accept variant identifiers because wishlist browsing is product-based.

Execute the insert in a transaction so validation failures leave the wishlist unchanged. Return the created wishlist item entity for immediate UI refresh.

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist item containing the saved product reference.

requestBody.description: Information required to save one product into the authenticated customer's wishlist.

operations.description:
Retrieve one saved wishlist item for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint returns the full wishlist item record identified by the path parameter and is intended for customer-facing wishlist detail views or refreshing a saved item from a browsing screen.

The server must verify that the requested wishlist item belongs to the current customer account. If the item does not exist or is not owned by the current customer, the request must be rejected according to the platform's authorization and privacy rules.

Wishlist items represent saved product interest at the product level. If the related product has been removed from the catalog, the wishlist item should still be handled as an owned saved record when present, while the client treats the product reference as unavailable rather than active catalog content.

This endpoint does not modify data, does not create snapshots, and does not alter wishlist contents.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Read the wishlist item from mall_platform_wishlist_items by its primary identifier. Confirm the authenticated customer owns the record before returning it. If the row is missing, return not found. If the row belongs to another customer, return not found or forbidden based on the platform's privacy conventions.

Keep the query read-only. Do not load unnecessary related rows unless the response serializer requires them. If a related product was deleted, do not fail the entire request solely because of the missing relation; return the wishlist item record when it still exists and let downstream consumers handle the missing catalog reference. Do not create snapshots or mutate any wishlist state.

responseBody.description: The saved wishlist item owned by the authenticated customer.

operations.description:
Remove one product entry from the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation deletes the selected wishlist item record while leaving the underlying product record unchanged. If the item has already been removed or no longer exists, the request is treated safely and the customer's remaining wishlist entries stay intact.

The removal applies only to the targeted wishlist item identified in the path. Wishlist maintenance rules also ensure that products deleted by sellers are removed automatically from wishlists elsewhere in the system, so this endpoint should not attempt to modify unrelated saved items or recreate missing entries.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the targeted row from mall_platform_wishlist_items by wishlistItemId after verifying the item belongs to the authenticated customer. If the item does not exist, treat the operation as a no-op and return success semantics consistent with idempotent deletion. Do not modify the product table or any other wishlist items.

Because this is customer-owned data, enforce ownership checks before deletion. If the item is found but belongs to another customer, reject the request with a forbidden or not-found style error according to the platform's authorization conventions. No snapshot is required for wishlist removals because the loaded snapshot rules do not include wishlists among the preserved change-history entities.

operations.description:
Searches the authenticated customer's order history.

This operation returns a paginated list of the customer's own orders. Each result includes the order number, placement date, total price, and the overall order status derived from its order items. The list is intended for browsing completed and in-progress purchases, so it shows summary information rather than full item-level details.

Filtering and sorting follow the platform browsing rules. Clients may narrow results by order status and date range and may sort by the supported order-history sort options. If there are no matching orders, the response returns an empty page rather than an error.

operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_orders for the authenticated customer only.
Apply pagination, optional filters, and sorting from the request body.
Use the derived overall order status from order items when producing each summary row, consistent with the order status rules.
Do not expose orders belonging to other customers.
Return a paginated summary projection for history browsing; do not return full order item or shipment detail here.
If the customer has no matching orders, return an empty page with valid pagination metadata.

operations.description:
Retrieves the full details of a single order.

This endpoint returns one persisted order record together with the data needed to display the customer-facing order detail page, including the shipping destination, item-level purchase history, and shipment information. Customers can only view their own orders, while sellers and administrators may access orders according to their oversight and fulfillment permissions.

The returned order should reflect preserved historical data rather than current catalog state, so item details, product information, variant information, and seller profile information remain stable even if the source records change later. If the order cannot be found, the service should return not found; if the caller is not allowed to view it, the service should return forbidden.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the order by its UUID and load all related data required for a full detail view. Enforce ownership so a customer can only access their own orders, while seller and administrator access follows platform authorization rules.

Include the preserved order items, the shipping address, and shipment data. For item-level history, return the stored purchase-time product and variant data together with the preserved seller profile information so historical review and dispute workflows remain accurate even after the underlying product or seller profile changes.

Do not expose other customers' orders. Return 404 when the order does not exist. Return 403 when the caller is authenticated but not allowed to view the order. This is a read-only operation and must not mutate any order, item, shipment, or snapshot data.

operations.description:
Search and paginate order items for operational browsing.

This endpoint returns a filtered list of purchased order items, including their quantity, status, and foreign-key references to the parent order, product variant, and seller. It is intended for seller dashboards and administrator review screens where order items must be found by status, order, seller, product variant, or creation time.

The result is paginated because order item lists can be large. Sorting and filtering must follow the platform browsing rules, and the service must return an empty page when no records match. This endpoint does not modify any data.

If a request contains invalid pagination values or unsupported filters, the service must reject it with a validation error.

operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_order_items with pagination, filtering, and sorting support.
Apply request filters to mall_platform_order_id, mall_platform_product_variant_id, mall_platform_seller_id, status, and created_at range as available in the request DTO.
Use indexed columns where possible, especially the composite indexes on order_id/status, seller_id/status, and product_variant_id/status, to keep the query efficient.

Customers use this view to inspect the progress of a specific purchase line even when other items in the same order have different statuses. Sellers and administrators use the same detail data to process fulfillment and review after-sales issues. If the item is missing or the caller is not allowed to access it, the service must return a normal business error response.

Join the related order, product, product variant, seller profile snapshot, shipment, cancellation request, refund request, and order-item snapshot data needed to render the full detail page.
Return the current item status together with the preserved purchase-context fields so the caller can see product name, variant, quantity, price, seller identity at purchase time, and shipment linkage.
Enforce access control so customers can read only their own order items, sellers can read order items belonging to their products, and administrators can read any order item.
If the order item does not exist or is not visible to the caller, return a standard not-found or forbidden business error.
Do not mutate order state, inventory, shipment, or request records in this operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single order item from a specific order.

This endpoint returns the live order item record for the requested order and item, including its current fulfillment status and relational context needed for item-level order history. It is intended for customers, sellers, and administrators when viewing or resolving order-item details.

Access is scoped to the parent order and must be authorized against the current user’s permissions. Customers may only access items from their own orders. Sellers may only access items for their own products, and administrators may access any order item for oversight or dispute resolution. If the order does not contain the requested item, the request must fail as not found.

For historical reconstruction and dispute review, the live order item is distinct from its immutable snapshot records. Snapshot data preserves the purchase-time product, variant, and seller presentation, while this endpoint returns the current operational state of the item.

Load the order by orderId first, then fetch the order item by orderItemId constrained to that order. Enforce authorization so customers can only read their own orders, sellers can only read order items belonging to their products, and administrators can read any order item.

Return the live order item entity from mall_platform_order_items. Do not attempt to reconstruct historical product or seller data from snapshots in this endpoint; the snapshot tables are for dispute/history use cases and should be accessed separately. Include the foreign-key identifiers and current status from the live record. If the order or order item has been deleted or is inaccessible under current permissions, respond with not found. No request body is needed.

operations.description:
Retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns preserved snapshot records for one order item within one order. It is intended for audit review, dispute resolution, and reconstruction of how the item changed over time. Snapshots are immutable and this operation only reads historical data.

The route is scoped by both the order and the order item so the history is always queried in the correct purchase context. Returned records should preserve the item state exactly as stored, including the preserved product, variant, and seller profile information captured when each snapshot was created. Pagination and sorting are supported because historical records can accumulate over time.

If the order exists but the item has no snapshots, the service should return an empty page. If the order does not exist or the item does not belong to the specified order, the service should return the platform's normal not-found response.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Verify that the order exists and that the order item belongs to that order before querying snapshots. Read from the immutable order item snapshot source using the order item identifier as the primary filter, and apply pagination and sorting from the request body. Default ordering should be newest-first unless another supported sort is requested.

Do not perform any write, update, or delete behavior because snapshots are immutable. Do not modify related orders or order items. If the order or order item is missing, return not found. If there are no snapshots for the item, return an empty page. The implementation should preserve the exact historical values captured in each snapshot and should not attempt to recalculate them from current data.

This operation exposes immutable historical data captured when the order item snapshot was created. The result is scoped by order, order item, and snapshot so the API can resolve the exact preserved option set for dispute review and order history reconstruction.

The returned records must reflect the exact state stored in the snapshot and must not be modified by this operation. If any parent resource does not exist, or if the snapshot does not belong to the specified order item, the request should fail with a not-found response. Access should follow the platform's historical record visibility rules so only authorized parties can inspect preserved order data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_order_item_snapshot_variant_options for the specified order, order item, and snapshot context.

First validate that the order exists, then confirm the order item belongs to that order, and finally confirm the snapshot belongs to that order item. After the parent chain is validated, load the option rows associated with the snapshot and return them in a stable order suitable for display and comparison.

Do not mutate any data. This endpoint is read-only and must not create, update, or delete snapshot data. If the caller is not authorized to view the preserved historical order data, return the appropriate authorization error. If any identifier is missing or the relationships do not match, return a not-found response rather than exposing unrelated snapshot rows.

operations.description:
Retrieve one historical variant option preserved inside an order item snapshot.

This endpoint returns the immutable option-value pair captured for the specified order item snapshot so consumers can reconstruct the purchased variant exactly as it existed at checkout time. It is intended for order history, audit, and dispute review flows where preserved purchase data must remain available even if the live product or variant changes later.

The request is scoped by order, order item, snapshot, and variant option identifiers. The server must verify that all identifiers belong to the same hierarchy before returning data. If the resource does not exist or the parent chain does not match, the server should return not found. Access should follow the platform's historical-order visibility rules so only authorized parties can view preserved purchase records.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the requested mall_platform_order_item_snapshot_variant_options record by variantOptionId and validate it belongs to the specified snapshot, order item, and order. Verify the parent chain using joins or sequential existence checks across mall_platform_orders, mall_platform_order_items, mall_platform_order_item_snapshots, and mall_platform_order_item_snapshot_variant_options.

Because this data is immutable historical snapshot content, do not perform any writes, do not regenerate snapshots, and do not modify related tables. Return 404 when any identifier is missing, mismatched, or inaccessible. Apply authorization checks based on the order-history and snapshot-viewing rules for the platform. Return the full entity using the canonical single-resource response component.

operations.description:
Search and list shipments with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

Shipments represent seller-specific delivery packages that may contain one or more order items from the same seller and share one set of tracking details. This endpoint is intended for order history screens, seller fulfillment views, and administrative browsing of shipment records.

Customers should only see shipments that belong to their own orders, sellers should only see shipments that contain their own order items, and administrators may browse all shipments. If the search matches no records, the response should be an empty page rather than an error.

Validation errors should be returned for unsupported filters, invalid pagination values, or malformed sorting rules. This endpoint does not modify shipment data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_shipments as the primary table and join mall_platform_shipment_items plus mall_platform_order_items when filtering by order scope, seller scope, or item membership. Apply pagination, keyword search, and sorting from the request body, then return shipment summary rows only.

Enforce actor-based visibility in the query layer: customers may only read shipments related to their own orders, sellers may only read shipments containing their own items, and administrators may read all shipments. Reject unsupported criteria, invalid page values, and impossible sort requests with validation errors rather than silently ignoring them.

Do not mutate any shipment rows in this operation. Completed shipments remain readable as historical records, but duplicate shipment creation or resubmission is outside the scope of this list endpoint.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of shipment summary records matching the search criteria.

requestBody.description: Shipment search criteria including pagination, sorting, and shipment-related filters.

operations.description:
Create a shipment for one seller's eligible order items.

This operation creates a new shipment package with shared tracking information and links the selected order items to it. It is used in the seller fulfillment workflow so customers can later view which items travel together inside the same shipment from their order history.

Every item in the shipment must belong to the same seller and must still be waiting to ship. If any selected item is already shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or assigned to another shipment, the request must fail and no shipment should be created. When creation succeeds, the included order items are updated to shipped status in the same transaction.

The response should include the created shipment and its linked items so the caller can immediately show tracking details. Validation errors should clearly identify missing tracking information, empty item selection, mixed-seller item selection, and duplicate or ineligible items.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Treat this as a transactional shipment-creation workflow.

Load the requested order items and verify that every item belongs to the authenticated seller. Reject the request if any item is not owned by that seller, if the items come from different sellers, or if any item is not in a shippable state.

Enforce the one-shipment-per-eligible-item rule. Before inserting anything, confirm that none of the selected items already belongs to an active shipment and that the same item is not duplicated in the request.

Create the shipment row and its shipment-item linkage rows in a single transaction. Persist the carrier name and tracking number from the request, then update all included order items to shipped status after the shipment is created.

Return the created shipment with its tracking fields and included order items. If validation fails, roll back the full transaction and return a domain error rather than creating a partial shipment.

responseBody.description: The shipment that was created, including its tracking information and included order items.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation details including the seller's eligible order items and the shipment tracking information.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipment with its tracking details and included order items.

This endpoint returns the shipment header for one package created by a seller, including carrier information, tracking number, shipment status, shipped and delivered timestamps, and the order items assigned to that shipment. It is used in order history and shipment detail views so customers can see how their items are grouped for delivery.

The shipment is identified by its UUID path parameter. The response should reflect the current shipment record together with its related shipment items so the consumer can display which order items travel together. If the shipment does not exist, return a not-found error. If the shipment belongs to an order the caller is not allowed to view, return an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by primary key and include its shipmentItems relation, with each linked orderItem and the minimal nested order-item references needed for display. Use a single transaction-free read query because this is a pure retrieval operation.

Validate that shipmentId is a UUID and return 404 when no shipment exists for the given id. Do not infer or compute shipment membership from orders; use the persisted shipment-item junction records. The response must expose current carrier_name, tracking_number, tracking_url, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, and updated_at values from mall_platform_shipments.

Preserve access control according to actor rules: customers may read shipments that belong to their own orders, sellers may read shipments for their own seller-owned orders/items, and administrators may read any shipment. If authorization fails, return 403. If the shipment has been deleted or is otherwise unavailable in persistence, treat it as not found.

responseBody.description: The full shipment record with related shipment items for display in order history and shipment detail views.

parameters.description: The shipment UUID identifier (global scope).
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Update a shipment's carrier, tracking information, or status.

This endpoint updates the shipment header for an existing seller shipment tied to a single order. It is used to correct carrier details, record tracking information, and advance shipment status as fulfillment progresses. Shipment membership is preserved, so the included order items are not reassigned by this operation.

The service must verify that the shipment exists, is not deleted, and is accessible to the caller according to seller ownership or administrator privileges. A completed shipment must not be reopened or resubmitted, and invalid lifecycle transitions must be rejected without partially updating the record. If the request changes the status to shipped or delivered, the corresponding timestamp fields should be populated when they are still empty.

If the shipment is not found, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks permission to modify it, return an authorization or ownership error. If the requested update conflicts with shipment lifecycle rules or tracking-number uniqueness within the seller scope, return a validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by id together with its seller, order, and shipmentItems relations. Verify that the caller is the owning seller or an administrator with shipment management privileges. Reject missing or deleted shipments.

Update only the shipment header fields exposed by the request body: carrier name, tracking number, tracking URL, and status. Never modify shipment item membership in this endpoint. Enforce the unique constraint on tracking_number combined with mall_platform_seller_id before persisting changes.

Disallow status changes that would reopen a shipment already marked delivered or otherwise completed. When transitioning to shipped, set shipped_at if it is null. When transitioning to delivered, set delivered_at if it is null. Keep the transaction atomic so the shipment record cannot be partially updated. Return the refreshed shipment after commit.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record including carrier, tracking, status, and fulfillment timestamps.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: The shipment fields that can be updated, including carrier information, tracking details, and status.

operations.description:
Delete a shipment record.

This endpoint removes a seller-specific shipment package identified by its UUID. It is intended for shipment lifecycle cleanup when a shipment must no longer be available in the active fulfillment flow.

The shipment belongs to one seller and one order, and it may have one or more shipment item assignments through the shipment-items relation. Implementations must verify the shipment exists before deletion and enforce business rules so that active fulfillment history is not corrupted. Because shipment items are linked by cascade relations, deleting the shipment should also remove its shipment-item assignments through the database relationship handling.

If the shipment does not exist, return a not-found error. If the shipment is already finalized or otherwise cannot be removed by policy, return a conflict or forbidden-style error according to the service error conventions.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Load the shipment by id and confirm it exists. Enforce authorization so only permitted seller/admin actors can delete it according to platform rules. Before deletion, consider the shipment status and prevent removal if the shipment is already delivered or otherwise locked by downstream business policy. Delete the shipment row and allow the database cascade to remove linked shipment-item rows. Do not modify order item records directly in this operation. Return a not-found error when the shipment id is invalid or missing, and map business rule violations to conflict/forbidden errors.

parameters.description: The shipment UUID to delete.
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Updates the order items assigned to a shipment.

This endpoint supports seller fulfillment by reconciling the membership of an existing shipment package. A shipment is the delivery unit for one seller, and every order item in that shipment must belong to the same seller and the same order. The server must validate those ownership and eligibility rules before applying any change.

The request is treated as the desired final set of order items for the shipment. The service should add missing shipment-item rows and remove rows that are no longer included, all inside one transaction. It must reject items that already belong to another shipment, items that belong to a different seller, items from a different order, or items that are not in a shippable state. If the resulting shipment would be empty, the request should be rejected.

Shipment header data such as carrier name, tracking number, tracking URL, shipped time, delivered time, and status must not be modified by this operation. Only the shipment-item junction table should change, and the update should fail atomically if any requested item is invalid.
operations.name: patchByShipmentid
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by id and verify that it exists and is not deleted. Use the shipment's seller id and order id as the validation scope.

Interpret the request body as the desired final set of order item identifiers for the shipment. Compare the requested set with the current mall_platform_shipment_items rows for that shipment. Insert missing rows and remove rows not present in the request within a single transaction.

For every requested order item, confirm that mall_platform_order_items.mall_platform_order_id matches the shipment's order, mall_platform_order_items.mall_platform_seller_id matches the shipment's seller, and the item is eligible for shipment. Also confirm that the item is not already assigned to another shipment-item row, since mall_platform_shipment_items enforces uniqueness on mall_platform_order_item_id. If any item fails validation, reject the entire request.

Do not update shipment carrier or status fields here. Do not allow cross-seller or cross-order composition. Reject requests that would leave the shipment with zero items if business rules require shipments to contain at least one order item. Return the updated shipment entity after commit.

responseBody.description: The shipment after its item membership has been updated.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier (UUID) whose item membership is being updated.
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: The desired final set of order item identifiers to include in the shipment.

operations.description:
Updates a shipment item assignment within a shipment.

This endpoint manages the junction record that associates one order item with one shipment. It is used to revise shipment membership while preserving the shipment header data such as carrier and tracking information.

The service must ensure that the specified shipment item belongs to the shipment identified by the path, that the related order item still belongs to the same seller as the shipment, and that the order item is not already assigned to another shipment. Any change that would violate shipment grouping rules, duplicate the order item assignment, or modify shipment header data must be rejected.

If the shipment item does not exist, the service returns a not found error. If the requested update would break delivery grouping constraints or item uniqueness, the service returns a validation or conflict error. Successful updates must be transactional and must refresh the record timestamps.

Load the shipment-item row by shipmentItemId and verify it belongs to shipmentId. Join the shipment and order item records to confirm the shipment and item share the same seller context and that the item remains eligible for assignment. Enforce the unique constraint on mall_platform_order_item_id so one order item cannot be linked to multiple shipments. If the update would move the item to a different shipment, verify the target shipment is also valid for that seller and has not violated any shipment state restrictions.

Use a transaction for the update to avoid race conditions with concurrent fulfillment actions. Do not update shipment carrier/tracking/status fields in this operation because those live on mall_platform_shipments, not on the junction table. If the platform forbids editing shipment membership after shipping or delivery, return a validation failure. Return the updated shipment-item record after persistence.

operations.description:
Remove one order item from a shipment.

This operation deletes the shipment-item association while leaving the shipment and the underlying order item intact. It is used to correct a shipment before fulfillment is finalized, such as when items need to be repacked or moved into a different seller-specific shipment.

The item must belong to the specified shipment, and the caller must be authorized to manage that shipment. If the shipment or shipment item does not exist, if the item belongs to another shipment, or if the shipment is locked by its lifecycle state, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found, forbidden, or conflict error.

Before deletion, check shipment state rules to ensure the shipment is still editable. Also ensure the deletion will not violate shipment integrity expectations; if the shipment must not become empty according to current business rules or implementation constraints, reject with a conflict.

Return a consistent error for missing shipment, missing shipment item, cross-shipment mismatch, unauthorized access, and locked shipment state. If the implementation returns a response body, it should be the refreshed shipment aggregate with remaining items and tracking information; otherwise return no content.

This endpoint lets a customer request cancellation for a specific purchased item instead of the entire order. The request is tied to one order item and carries the customer's reason for review by the item's seller.

The request is accepted only when the target order item belongs to the authenticated customer, is still in paid status, and has not been shipped. If the item is unavailable for cancellation, the system rejects the request without changing the order item, sibling items, inventory, or any existing cancellation history.

On success, create a new cancellation request row bound to exactly one order item and persist the customer-provided reason and initial pending review state. Do not update the order item status, inventory, shipments, or any sibling order items here; those effects occur only after seller review. Return the created cancellation request entity.
